history.summary: FLAG - INTERFAITH SITE, not a Hindu-only temple: Sri Surya Pahar, about 13 km southeast of Goalpara, is a hilly archaeological landscape (c. 1 sq km) where Hindu, Buddhist and Jain remains coexist. Hindu remains include hundreds of rock-cut Shiva lingams scattered over the hills, low-relief figures of Surya, Vishnu and Ardhanarisvara, and the stone-paved Ganesh kunda stream; Buddhist remains include rock-cut monolithic stupas (earliest phase c. 100 BC-100 AD), votive stupas and an excavated monastic complex; Jain remains include rock-cut figures of Tirthankaras Adinath and Neminath under a rock shelter, plus remains of brick and stone temples. Local tradition credits Vyasa with carving 99,999 lingams to make a second Kashi (traditional claim, not an archaeological count). The ASI excavated the site over nine seasons in 1992-2001 (archaeologist K. K. Muhammed); the site has been under ASI protection since the 1960s and has a site museum. Nearby Dekdhuwa Pahar and Mahadev Pahar (protected by the Directorate of Archaeology, Assam) share the same complex character. town_description: Goalpara, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra in western Assam, is the headquarters of Goalpara district and a gateway town between Upper Assam and the North Bengal hills. Its surroundings hold one of Assam's richest archaeological clusters, led by Sri Surya Pahar.
